title: Maximum Difference Between Even and Odd Frequency II
summary: Given a string s and an integer k, find the maximum difference between the frequency of an odd-frequency character and a non-zero even-frequency character in any substring of at least k characters.
statement: Given a string s and an integer k, find the maximum difference between the frequency of an odd-frequency character and a non-zero even-frequency character in any substring of at least k characters. The substring can include more than two distinct characters.
constraints: s has 3–30,000 digits from 0 through 4 and k is at least one.
Choose a substring of length at least k and two distinct digits: the first has odd frequency and the second has positive even frequency.
Maximize first frequency minus second frequency.
hints: For a fixed ordered digit pair, prefix-count parities identify valid odd/even frequency differences.
Scan right endpoints while retaining the smallest eligible prefix difference for each parity pair.
Release prefixes only after the length bound and two occurrences of the even digit; query the opposite odd parity and same even parity.
Subtracting the minimum compatible prefix maximizes the frequency difference, and enumerating 20 ordered pairs covers every choice.
editorial: Subtracting the minimum compatible prefix maximizes the frequency difference, and enumerating 20 ordered pairs covers every choice.

tests.explanation: Among qualifying substrings and digit pairs, the largest valid difference is negative one.
The full string has digit two once and each of zero and one twice, producing difference negative one.
